svg.text: Restaurant Rush: Stage 2 class diagram (tag stage-2)
All 35 classes of the stage-2 code, with every member and every relationship checked against the compiled classes of that tag.
- create(CustomerType, int, String, int, int): Customer
both for live play and ScriptedInput
Every field is private and there are no setters.
lockedPriceCents is final: the price is fixed when the order
is taken. status changes only through advancePreparation,
markServed, markPaid and cancel, and each one throws
IllegalStateException when called out of order.
Restaurant creates its Tables and its WaitingQueue in its own
constructor, so they exist only inside it. The Menu and the
three staff members are created in RestaurantRush and
passed in, which makes those aggregations.
createOrderFor(...) asks the customer rather than testing its
time, so a CriticCustomer picks the most demanding dish and
subclass loses its own amount per turn (8, 5,
association: navigable, the source holds a field
association: both ends hold a field
aggregation: whole holds parts made elsewhere
composition: whole creates and owns its parts
orange border: class added in stage 2
+ public - private # protected ~ package. Underlined: static. Italic:
Role names on the lines are the Java field names. Parameters show
Not listed: constructors, toString(), and getters that only return a field.
Dependencies left out to keep lines apart
RestaurantRush creates and wires every object; only its «create» of
ArrivalSchedule creates the RegularCustomer, VIPCustomer and
CriticCustomer that it returns as Customer.
Money (static helpers for cents) is used by MenuItem, Order,
Any other parameter or return type can be read in the operation
